svg.title: Pinecone SDK layered architecture
svg.desc: Four strict unidirectional horizontal layers: Public API entry point, Namespace/domain operations, Transport/HTTP and adapters, Configuration and models. Each layer depends only downward; no lower layer imports from an upper layer.

g.onclick: sendPrompt('Who calls the Pinecone SDK public API?')

g.text: Caller-facing surface — owns no HTTP logic, composes namespace objects and delegates

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What does pinecone/_client.py Pinecone class do?')
sendPrompt('What does AsyncPinecone add over Pinecone?')
sendPrompt('What does the Admin client expose?')

g.text: Business logic per domain — calls HTTP client below, delegates response parsing to adapters

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What does pinecone/client/indexes.py Indexes class do?')
sendPrompt('What does pinecone/index/__init__.py Index class do?')

svg.text: pinecone/async_client/ mirrors all namespaces above with async equivalents

g.text: Dependency-only — no namespace-level business logic resides here

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What does HTTPClient in pinecone/_internal/http_client.py do?')

g.text: Pure data structures and utilities — no outbound I/O, no upward imports

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What does PineconeConfig and RetryConfig contain?')
sendPrompt('What typed response models live in pinecone/models/?')
sendPrompt('What do vector_factory.py and validation.py do?')

svg.text: Strictly unidirectional — no lower layer imports from an upper layer anywhere in the codebase
